rule.description: Credential Access: unprivileged read attempt on /etc/shadow (denied)

full_log: type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1787839633.189:156668): arch=c000003e syscall=257 success=no exit=-13 comm="cat" exe="/usr/bin/cat" subj=unconfined key="shadow_access" AUID="normann" UID="normann" EUID="normann" type=CWD msg=audit(1787839633.189:156668): cwd="/home/normann/portfolio-checkout" type=PATH msg=audit(1787839633.189:156668): item=0 name="/etc/shadow" inode=10227249 dev=08:07 mode=0100640 ouid=0 ogid=42 OUID="root" OGID="shadow"
_note: Real auditd alert for Scripts/linux-simulations.sh credential-access, run on 2026-08-27 as the unprivileged user normann. cat: /etc/shadow: Permission denied on the terminal confirms the read was genuinely denied (exit=-13 = EACCES), which is exactly the T1003.008 signal - the attempt being denied, not whether it succeeded. Building this rule surfaced a real false-positive source: sudo itself reads /etc/shadow internally on every authentication (PAM's pam_unix module checking the password hash), tripping the same auditd watch key with audit.success=yes and audit.command=sudo - requiring audit.success=no in the rule excludes that legitimate case. Captured verbatim via `docker exec single-node-wazuh.manager-1 grep "100220" /var/ossec/logs/alerts/alerts.json`, no content altered.
